cards.text: This prophecy comes from the book of Zechariah, a prophet (Zechariah 1:1), and it speaks about Jerusalem. It opens, "Behold, a day of the LORD is coming when your plunder will be divided in your presence." Then it says, "For I will gather all the nations for battle against Jerusalem…"

cards.question: All the nations will come for battle against Jerusalem. What will happen to the city?

cards.text: The houses will be looted, and the women ravished. But remember how this prophecy opened: the plunder divided "in your presence."

cards.question: When Jerusalem is captured, some of its people will still be left in the city.

cards.text: Half of the city will go into exile, but the rest of the people will stay. Then somebody will go out to fight against those nations.

cards.question: Who will go out to fight against the nations that came against Jerusalem?

cards.text: On that day the LORD's feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem, and the mountain will split in two from east to west, forming a great valley. Half of it will move north and half south, and friend, this is the kind of news I'd need to sit down for, if I had anything to sit down WITH.

cards.question: A great valley will open through the Mount of Olives, right next to a city under attack. What does the prophecy say people will do there?

cards.text: The valley will reach to a place called Azal, and the flight will be like the one from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah, king of Judah. Then the LORD will come, and He won't come alone.

cards.question: When the LORD comes, who will come with Him?

cards.text: On that day there will be no light, no cold or frost. "It will be a unique day known only to the LORD, without day or night…"

cards.question: On that unique day, when evening comes, it will get dark like any other evening.

cards.text: And on that day living water will flow out from Jerusalem, half toward the Eastern Sea and half toward the Western Sea. Now it's not just the land that's changing, friend.

cards.question: The living water from Jerusalem will flow in summer and winter alike.

cards.text: Now here comes the line I'd frame and hang over every oven in my bakery. It's about who rules over all the earth.

cards.question: On that day the LORD will become ___ over all the earth.
On that day the LORD will share His rule over the earth with the gods of the nations.

cards.text: It's "the LORD alone, and His name alone." King over ALL the earth, and me? I'm in charge of one little cookie planet, and my oven STILL doesn't listen to me.

All the land from Geba to Rimmon, south of Jerusalem, will be turned into a plain, but Jerusalem will be raised up and will remain in her place, from gate to gate and tower to winepresses. The land south of it will go flat and Jerusalem will RISE, like the one cookie in my batch that actually puffs up right.

cards.question: Even after being raised up, Jerusalem will face utter destruction again someday.

cards.text: People will live there, and Jerusalem will dwell securely. Then the prophecy turns to the plague with which the LORD will strike all the peoples who have warred against Jerusalem.
This part is heavy, friend. Their flesh will rot while they stand on their feet, their eyes will rot in their sockets, and their tongues will rot in their mouths.

cards.question: On that day a great panic from the LORD will come on the peoples who warred against Jerusalem. What will they do?

answers.text: They will turn on each other
They will grow calm and wait
They will make peace with Judah

cards.text: Judah will also fight at Jerusalem, and remember the plunder divided at the very start? This time the prophecy turns to the wealth of all the surrounding nations.

cards.question: Judah will fight at Jerusalem. What will happen to the wealth of all the surrounding nations?

answers.text: It will be collected in great abundance
It will be scattered across the land
It will all be sent back home

cards.text: A similar plague will strike the horses and mules, camels and donkeys, and all the animals in those camps. Then comes a turn I did NOT see coming, and it's about the survivors from those same nations.

cards.question: Year after year, what will the survivors from the nations that came against Jerusalem go up to do?
Year after year, the survivors will go up to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts. Which feast will they celebrate?
If any of the families of the earth don't go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, then the ___ will not fall on them.

cards.text: Egypt gets named too: if its people won't go up, the rain won't fall on them either, and this will be the punishment of Egypt and of all the nations that don't go up. Then, on that day, even ordinary things will be set apart for the LORD, starting with words inscribed on the bells of the horses.

cards.question: On that day, ___ TO THE LORD will be inscribed on the bells of the horses.

cards.text: The cooking pots in the house of the LORD will be like the sprinkling bowls before the altar, and every pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the LORD of Hosts. EVERY POT, friend, and I thought going from the back of a junk drawer to a gold base was a big glow-up.
All who sacrifice will come and take some of those pots and cook in them. Holy bells, holy pots, and there's one last line about the house of the LORD of Hosts.

cards.question: On that day, there will no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the LORD of Hosts.
